audit: DYK No. 01 'Time, Compressed' — frame-by-second sync / SFX / continuity audit (read-only)
method: All 48 contact sheets (574 frames, 1 fps) reviewed in order against timeline-by-second.txt and the Tc*.tsx cue sources.

Sampling note: frames were extracted with ffmpeg fps=1 (round=near), so the tile labelled N:SS shows the picture at about N:SS + 0.47 s. Every 'empty frame' finding was cross-checked against the exact cue math (build_final.py START/VO_AT + makeCue) and matches the sources.
Exact SFX times come from the CUES list in build_final.py (computed, not guessed); exact word times from vo.json + timeline.json.
Near-empty frames were also detected numerically (bright-pixel count in the picture area, HUD excluded).

findings.what_you_see: After the 1883 header docks, the picture is empty (docked year + HUD only) for about 2 s. Tiles 4:10 and 4:11 have no content at all. The NOON clock rises only at 4:12.0.
findings.what_you_hear: 'At midday, the church clock strikes twelve' (250.18–252.24 s). The chime-reward comes on 'twelve'.
findings.why_its_wrong: The screen is blank for 2 s while the narrator describes a specific object (the church clock). This breaks the 'no empty ≥2 s while narration describes something' rule.
findings.suggested_fix: In Tc1800.tsx, key the noon clock to C.at('midday') (or 'church') instead of NOON='twelve'. Set p2 = ease(f, MIDDAY-8, MIDDAY+6) and rise(f, MIDDAY-4), about 1.8 s earlier. Keep chime-reward on 'twelve' and pulse the hand or flash the clock rim on NOON so the chime still has a visual hit.

findings.what_you_see: After the 1914 header docks, the picture is empty for about 2 s (tiles 5:13 and 5:14 are blank). The factory and queue appear only at 5:15.0.
findings.what_you_hear: 'Outside Ford's factory, the line of people looking for work…' (313.62–317.44 s). wind-soft plays on 'line' (315.18).
findings.why_its_wrong: The screen is blank while the narrator names Ford's factory. This is the same defect pattern as H1.
findings.suggested_fix: In Tc1900.tsx, start <Queue> at C.at('Outside') (313.62), about 1.5 s earlier than LINE. Show the factory block first and let the people stagger in from 'line', so wind-soft keeps its cue.

findings.what_you_see: The answer beat opens on an empty dark frame. Only a tiny '★ THE ANSWER' kicker appears at 6:45.3. 'Time did not speed up.' rises at 6:46.2. Tiles 6:44 and 6:45 are blank.
findings.what_you_hear: 'Here is the answer.' A loud impact-deep-soft (0.48) hits on 'answer' at 6:45.51. Two whoosh-reverse cues also play 1 s apart (6:43.2 era exit and 6:44.17 shot start).
findings.why_its_wrong: One of the film's biggest hits lands on a blank screen at the episode's turning point. The doubled reverse whoosh adds sound with nothing on screen.
findings.suggested_fix: In TcReveal.tsx, bring a big 'THE ANSWER' title (or the headline) in at ANSWER-6 so it slams on the impact. Then hand over to 'Time did not speed up.' at SPEED-8. In build_final.py, drop the Tc2000 era-exit whoosh-reverse (end-0.95) because TcReveal already opens with one.

findings.what_you_see: The phone mock-up (with its red '12' badge) fades in on top of the still-centred 'YOU WAKE UP IN / Today' header. The dark phone body blacks out 'WAKE UP' and the 'To' of 'Today', so the header looks broken. About 0.9 s later the DYK card covers the phone and it is gone.
findings.what_you_hear: '…you have already checked your phone.' Three pop-reveals play at 6:04.84, 6:05.19 and 6:05.54, then ui-toggle and chime for the DYK card.
findings.why_its_wrong: Two elements collide and mask the episode's era title. The phone is also a flash element (under 1 s, then covered).
findings.suggested_fix: In Tc2000.tsx, dock the header earlier (dockAt = C.at('Before') + 4, about 362.7 s). Start <Glow> at C.at('already') - 4 so the phone holds for about 1.5 s on its own after the dock. Also delay DidYouKnowThat by about 10 frames (at = DID + 10) or fade the phone out under the card instead of hard-covering it.

findings.what_you_see: The cliffhanger band 'They lost their Monday. Next, steam takes noon itself.' appears at 3:57.0 and stays on screen.
findings.what_you_hear: 'Workers had lost their Monday. In the next century, the steam engine… would take something even bigger.' The punchline 'Noon itself.' only comes at 4:03.69.
findings.why_its_wrong: The on-screen text gives away the narrator's scripted reveal 6.7 s early, so the spoken punchline lands flat.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the band to 'They lost their Monday. Next, steam takes something bigger…', or keep the text and reveal 'noon itself.' at C.at('Noon'): render the last two words with opacity ease(f, NOON-4, NOON+6) inside the Cliffhanger children.

findings.what_you_see: For about 4 s a small green 'TIME SAVED' arrow sits alone, left of centre, on an otherwise black frame. The invisible 'yet' and hourglass still take up flex space, so the arrow is pushed off-centre.
findings.what_you_hear: 'We have saved more time than any generation in history.'
findings.why_its_wrong: The frame looks broken or unbalanced, is nearly empty for 4 s, and comes in the cold open where retention matters most.
findings.suggested_fix: Centre the arrow on its own until 'So' (for example translateX that eases from +300 px to 0 over SOWHY-4…SOWHY+8), or reserve the space visibly with a faint outline of the hourglass slot. Optionally add a counter or year tick under the arrow on 'generation' so the 4 s are not static.

findings.what_you_see: The cut from the 'LET'S BEGIN' pill is to a pure black frame (1:02.3–1:03.4), then only a tiny 'THE EXPERIMENT' kicker until 'Seven centuries.' and the timeline arrive at 1:05.0. Tiles 1:02–1:04 are empty.
findings.what_you_hear: 'Here is the experiment. Seven…' A whoosh-wind plays at the cut (62.33).
findings.why_its_wrong: The screen is nearly empty for about 2.7 s at the start of the promise beat while the narrator introduces it.
findings.suggested_fix: In TcPromise.tsx, draw the Timeline7 axis (line only, nodes later) from frame 0. Add a large 'THE EXPERIMENT' heading on EXP (C.at('experiment')) that shrinks into the kicker when 'Seven centuries.' arrives.

findings.what_you_see: The timeline, the person icons and the 'IN EACH ONE you wake up as someone else' chip stay unchanged for about 5.8 s.
findings.what_you_hear: '…else, and see how people really lived with time. By the end, you will know exactly…'
findings.why_its_wrong: Nothing new appears for more than 5 s while the narration moves on.
findings.suggested_fix: On C.at('lived') (74.64), light the seven person icons in sequence (ui-click-soft at 0.15, 4 frames apart), or show a small 'HOW PEOPLE LIVED WITH TIME' line. Move 'WHERE DID THE TIME GO?' to C.at('where') (78.07): it is already close, so only the extra beat is needed.

findings.what_you_see: Each cliffhanger band shows its full sentence as soon as the cliffhanger starts. 1500 shows 'A strange new drink is on its way…' at 2:11.1. 1600 shows 'Soon the minute stops being a curiosity — and becomes your boss.' at 3:00.8.
findings.what_you_hear: 1500: 'strange new drink' at 2:13.4 (2.3 s later). 1600: 'Nobody noticed what that meant.' first, then 'the minute would stop being a curiosity… your boss' at 3:02.7–3:07.1 (up to 6.3 s later).
findings.why_its_wrong: The text runs more than 1 s ahead of the words it states and pre-empts the narrator's teaser.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the Cliffhanger band (and the piano) on the first word, but key its text to the matching phrase. For 1500, use a text-reveal at C.at('strange'). For 1600, start the text at C.at('Within') (182.67) or show 'Nobody noticed what that meant.' first and swap on 'Within'. A generic fix is to give Cliffhanger a textAt prop separate from at.

findings.what_you_see: Each cliffhanger dims the whole scene (by 60–75%) and then holds a static frame for 7–8 s. In 1700 nothing at all moves for 8 s.
findings.what_you_hear: The teaser narration continues throughout (for example 'the steam engine, racing on iron rails, would take something even bigger').
findings.why_its_wrong: These are dead stretches over 5 s at every era exit, which is exactly where the open loop should pull hardest.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one motion element per cliffhanger, keyed to its noun: a coffee cup silhouette on 'drink' (134.06); the minute hand sweeping faster and a 'BOSS' stamp on 'boss' (187.06); a train crossing the band on 'steam' / 'rails' (239.30–240.82) with a soft rail-clack. Each element needs its own SFX.

findings.what_you_see: The newspaper stack and 'news becomes a habit' sit unchanged on the left half for about 6 s. The right half of the frame is empty from 2:37 to 2:48.
findings.what_you_hear: '…people wanted to know what happened today, not last month. Then, in 1656, Christiaan Huygens…'
findings.why_its_wrong: This is a dead stretch, and 'today vs last month' (the beat's actual point) is never shown.
findings.suggested_fix: On C.at('today') (163.78), put a 'TODAY' chip beside a struck-through 'LAST MONTH' chip (strike on C.at('month') at 165.27) in the empty right half, each with a soft pop.

findings.what_you_see: In the Week Strip, the 'SAINT MONDAY' tag sits directly under the 'A WEEK IN 1760' heading, about 1 px apart. It reads as a sub-heading, not as a tag on the MON bar.
findings.what_you_hear: 'Back then, you worked hard when there was work to do…'
findings.why_its_wrong: The text collides and the tag's meaning is lost (it labels MON).
findings.suggested_fix: In WeekStrip (dykkit.tsx), put tags in their own row at least 24 px below the heading, or inside the bar. The 1850 strip at 4:29 ('FREE FROM 2 PM', 'REST') shows the correct spacing.

findings.what_you_see: The 1850 Week Strip stays unchanged for about 7 s after the 'FREE FROM 2 PM' tag.
findings.what_you_hear: 'Soon, the men got the same. Even free time had to be written into law.'
findings.why_its_wrong: This is a dead stretch, and 'the men got the same' / 'written into law' are not shown.
findings.suggested_fix: On C.at('men') (271.39), add a second row of figures or a 'MEN TOO' tag. On C.at('law') (274.64), stamp a small 'FACTORY ACT 1850' seal (stamp-hit at 0.3).

findings.what_you_see: Only the 1870 bar (3,000+ h/yr) is on screen for about 6.5 s. The 'RECENTLY · GERMANY · 2017 / 1,354' bar appears only at 6:22.1.
findings.what_you_hear: 'In Germany recently, it was around thirteen hundred and fifty' starts at 6:19.75.
findings.why_its_wrong: The Germany bar is 2.3 s late against its first spoken word (the limit is 1.5 s), which also leaves a 6.5 s static hold.
findings.suggested_fix: In Tc2000.tsx, change the second Bar to at={GERMANY - 4} (379.6 s). Its counter then runs over 'recently… thirteen hundred and fifty'. Move the ui-click from 'fifty' to 'Germany' in build_final.py.

findings.what_you_see: 'Each one saved time. Each one made our hours look more alike.' appears as one line at 7:25.1, after both sentences have been spoken.
findings.what_you_hear: 'Each invention saved us time.' at 7:20.76. 'And each one made our hours look more and more the same.' at 7:22.99–7:25.45.
findings.why_its_wrong: The text is 4.3 s late against the start of the sentence it states.
findings.suggested_fix: Split it into two rises: 'Each one saved time.' at C.at('invention') - 4 (441.0), and 'Each one made our hours look more alike.' at C.at('made') - 4 (443.7). Keep the sameness bar dimming as it is.

findings.what_you_see: The Goldman and four-day-week cards and the network stay static for about 6.5 s.
findings.what_you_hear: '…fifty six of them kept it. Put those facts together, and the fifteen hour week that Keynes…'
findings.why_its_wrong: This is a dead stretch over 5 s, and 'put those facts together' is not shown.
findings.suggested_fix: On C.at('together') (474.49), pull the three evidence cards together (scale or slide inward, soft whoosh). On C.at('fifteen') (475.68), bring the Keynes card in about 1.2 s earlier than KEYNES.

findings.what_you_see: After the cut, only a tiny 'DID YOU KNOW THAT? · NO. 01' label is on an otherwise empty frame for about 3.2 s. 'Time, Compressed' appears at 8:31.8.
findings.what_you_hear: 'This was episode one of Did You Know That. Time, Compressed.' (509.17–512.21).
findings.why_its_wrong: The screen is nearly empty for more than 2 s while the channel is named, and the brand gets no visual.
findings.suggested_fix: In TcOutro.tsx, show the DytLogoAnimated plus wordmark (or a large 'DID YOU KNOW THAT?' lockup) on C.at('Did') (510.57) and the title on 'episode' (509.69). Shrink both into the current header position when 'turn' arrives.

findings.what_you_see: After the COMMENT OF THE WEEK chip, part 1 is static for about 9.7 s. After the Dexty.live pill it is static again for about 8.6 s, until 'Like'.
findings.what_you_hear: 'I will read the best comment, right here, on this screen. And the subject you ask for most becomes a future episode.' and later '…watch every episode, collect the facts, and play the guessing game. If this changed how you see a single hour,'
findings.why_its_wrong: Two dead stretches of about 9 s each. Three SFX in the first stretch (impact-soft 8:44.35, pop-reveal 8:47.59, sparkle-soft 8:50.62) have nothing on screen.
findings.suggested_fix: Give each SFX a reveal: 'COMMENT OF THE WEEK' on 'deal' (524.35); a pointer or frame flash on 'right here' (528.47); a 'SUBJECT → EPISODE' chip on 'subject' (530.62). On the Dexty pill, reveal 'WATCH · COLLECT · PLAY' word by word on 'watch' (537.41), 'collect' (539.10) and 'play' (540.44).

findings.what_you_see: 'yet', the hourglass and the 'RUNNING OUT' label appear at 0:15.8–0:16.3.
findings.what_you_hear: 'So why does every one of us feel like we are running out of it?' 'running' comes at 0:18.57, with clock-tick-soft.
findings.why_its_wrong: The 'RUNNING OUT' label is 2.1 s early, and the hourglass entrance has no sound.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the hourglass at SOWHY+4 but fade the 'RUNNING OUT' label in at RUNNING-4. Optionally add a soft pop on the hourglass entrance.

findings.shot: TcIntro→TcWelcome, TcWelcome, Tc1600, Tc1900→Tc2000, Tc2000, Tc2100→TcClose
findings.what_you_see: Brief dips to an empty background or black at crossfades and joins. The title card cuts to 11 frames of empty navy before the welcome lockup. Fade-out-then-fade-in passes through empty at 0:36 / 0:59 / 2:36 / 6:13. The 3-frame shot fade gives a fully black sample at 6:00.47. TcClose opens on about 0.5 s of black.
findings.what_you_hear: Narration continues across each dip ('Welcome', 'with a question', 'Ready?', 'The first newspaper', 'Time').
findings.why_its_wrong: These are micro-blinks that a careful viewer reads as stutters, not intentional cuts.
findings.suggested_fix: Overlap the crossfades so the incoming panel starts 4–6 frames before the outgoing one ends (for example in TcWelcome, p1b in at QUESTION-10 instead of QUESTION-4). In TcWelcome, start the lockup at frame 0 (WELCOME-15). In TcClose, rise 'Time cannot be slowed down.' at SLOWED-24 so it is up on frame 0. Consider useShotFade(inF=0) on cuts where the neighbours share a background.

findings.what_you_see: Nothing new appears at these moments. The GUESS card has been on screen since 0:54.5. The Day Clock is static at 2:33–2:34. Both noon clocks are already up at 4:16. The 1926 pill only arrives at 5:35.8. There is no scribble animation at 9:19.
findings.what_you_hear: pop-reveal on 'comments', page-flip on 'read', knock-solid on 'argue', knock-solid on 'twice', warm-shimmer on 'Saturdays', pencil-scribble.
findings.why_its_wrong: Each SFX has no visible reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop these cues or add a micro-visual. Pulse the '↓' on GUESS at 'comments'. Flash the coffeehouse segment of the 1652 Day Clock at 'read'/'argue'. Flash both noon clocks at 'twice'. Move the 1926 pill to C.at('Saturdays') - 4. Animate the ✎ glyph at 9:19.6.

findings.what_you_see: The frame is static (the dimmed cliffhanger) for the last second before each cut.
findings.what_you_hear: A whoosh-reverse 0.95 s before every cut, then whoosh-wind and impact-soft on the cut.
findings.why_its_wrong: The reverse whoosh 'sucks' over a frozen picture. At 6:43/6:44 two reverse whooshes play back to back.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 0.9 s visual pull-in to each era exit (scale 1→1.04 and fade toward the cut, starting at end-28 frames) so the reverse whoosh has motion. Remove the Tc2000 exit whoosh (see H3).

findings.what_you_see: Major scene changes with no sound: the village, Harrison's map and clock, the four time-zone bars, the Beard book, the 'One life. Born 1900.' timeline (its whoosh comes 2 s later on 'three'), the Keynes card, 'Your brain…', the Holiday Paradox week tiles, and 'Every century…'.
findings.what_you_hear: Only narration and the music bed.
findings.why_its_wrong: A big visual change with no matching SFX is inconsistent with the rest of the film, where most reveals have one.
findings.suggested_fix: Add soft cues (gain 0.2–0.3) on each reveal word: whoosh-soft on 'Your' (102.55), 'Harrison's' (226.26) and 'child' (337.72); ui-click ×4 on 'railroads'; page-flip on 'George' (287.05) and 'Keynes' (351.39); warm-shimmer on 'holiday'; ui-click ×7 on 'week' (423.77); whoosh-soft on 'Every' (431.00).

findings.what_you_see: The 'news arrives' card is still up during 'Time is not…'. The right half is empty at 2:08.4. 'Time is not something you spend.' appears at 2:08.5.
findings.what_you_hear: 'Time is not something you spend.' (127.41–128.72).
findings.why_its_wrong: The line appears 1.1 s after it starts, with a dip to empty in between.
findings.suggested_fix: In Tc1500.tsx, key phase C to C.at('Time') (127.41) instead of 'spend' (phaseB out at TIME-14, phaseC in at TIME-2).

findings.what_you_see: 'BY CABLE ≈ 16 HOURS' and 'Fifteen times faster.' appear while the 'BY SHIP ≈ 10 DAYS' row above is still an empty gap. The ship baseline arrives at 4:42.8.
findings.what_you_hear: '…took sixteen hours to send, instead of ten days by ship.'
findings.why_its_wrong: The comparison claim appears before its baseline. 'Fifteen times faster' is never spoken.
findings.suggested_fix: Move rise of 'Fifteen times faster.' to C.at('ship') + 6 (about 283.7 s) so it lands after both bars are on screen.

findings.what_you_see: 'Complaining about speed — a century before your phone.' appears at 5:02.7. 'One lifetime now holds more change than whole centuries once did.' appears at 5:46.5.
findings.what_you_hear: 'People were complaining…' from 4:58.68. 'One lifetime now holds…' from 5:44.42.
findings.why_its_wrong: The text is 2–4 s behind the start of the sentence it states (keyed to the last noun).
findings.suggested_fix: Key them to C.at('People') - 2 (298.6) and C.at('lifetime') - 6 (344.5).

findings.what_you_see: The 'THE HUMAN MIND' label fills its 360 px card edge to edge, with almost no inner padding.
findings.what_you_hear: 'The human mind.'
findings.why_its_wrong: Text is cramped against the neon border and the card looks inconsistent with the other three.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap it to two lines ('THE HUMAN' / 'MIND') or use fontSize 28 with padding 0 20px.

findings.what_you_see: When the sun is up, the village sky gradient shows as a visible rectangle with a hard top edge. The mask only fades the left, right and bottom.
findings.what_you_hear: 'Your day begins when the sun rises, and ends when it sets.'
findings.why_its_wrong: A hard box edge reads as a rendering artefact.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a top fade to the Village mask, for example linear-gradient(180deg, transparent, black 15%, black 92%, transparent).

findings.what_you_see: 'Your brain measures time in' sits as an unfinished sentence on a nearly empty frame for about 3.4 s until 'memories.' appears.
findings.what_you_hear: 'Your brain does not measure time with a clock. It measures it with memories.'
findings.why_its_wrong: The dangling half-sentence and empty frame do not match the VO's 'not with a clock' beat.
findings.suggested_fix: Show a small clock icon struck through on C.at('clock', 1) (418.38), then reveal 'memories.' as now.

findings.what_you_see: Only the small 'How are you?' bubble in the upper left. The rest of the frame is empty for about 4 s.
findings.what_you_hear: '…ask anyone how they are, and you will hear the same word.'
findings.why_its_wrong: The frame is nearly empty (intentional tension, but long).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a typing indicator ('…') in the reply position from C.at('same') (398.96) up to 'Busy'.

findings.what_you_see: The 1500 header card holds static for about 5 s.
findings.what_you_hear: 'It is midnight. Pitch black. And the whole village is awake.'
findings.why_its_wrong: This is borderline dead, and 'the whole village is awake' (the era's sensory hook) is not shown.
findings.suggested_fix: On C.at('awake') (89.12), light a few window glows in a dark village silhouette behind the header before it docks.

findings.what_you_see: A very dim skyline plus the header and PREDICTION label. The picture area is almost empty for about 4 s.
findings.what_you_hear: 'Now, the year 2100. That morning has not happened yet. But we can follow the evidence.'
findings.why_its_wrong: The frame is nearly empty and low-contrast at the start of the final era.
findings.suggested_fix: Raise skyline window opacity (0.5 → 0.8) and show 'THE EVIDENCE · REAL DATA' on 'follow' (456.11) a little larger.

findings.what_you_see: For about 1 s, the HUD year counter rolls through intermediate years (1621, 1759, 1871, 1891, 2019). At 7:31.5 the HUD reads 2026 while the big header says 2100.
findings.what_you_hear: 'You wake up in…'
findings.why_its_wrong: For a moment the HUD contradicts the header. This is intentional, but it is a visible inconsistency.
findings.suggested_fix: Finish the HUD roll before the header slam completes (roll over 12 frames from shot start), or keep the HUD hidden until the header docks.

findings.what_you_see: The time-discipline panel stays static. Nothing refers to Saint Monday.
findings.what_you_hear: 'Saint Monday begins to disappear.' (221.96–223.36)
findings.why_its_wrong: A named idea is spoken with no visual for about 4.8 s.
findings.suggested_fix: Bring back a small 'SAINT MONDAY' chip and fade or strike it on 'disappear' (223.36), with a soft trap-snap.

clean_stretches: 0:00–0:11 hook split screen: every element lands on its word, with knock, send and pop matched
0:37–0:45 ?→! and the four category pops, all on their words
0:51–1:01.5 THE RULE (GUESS, STAY, CHECK stamps on their words), Ready?, LET'S BEGIN
1:29.5–1:41 1500 DYK card and Day Clock (7 ticks match the draw-on)
2:00–2:06 SAME TOOLS / ROADS / NEWS stamps and the weeks-late bar
2:48–3:00 Huygens clock, pendulum tick, 15 min→15 s flip, the minute
3:28–3:41 field→factory, SUN→BELL→CLOCK chain, time discipline, the strike-through on 'says'
4:52–4:58 Beard's three suspects and 'Sound familiar?' with phone
5:27–5:36 assembly line 12 h 30 → 93 min and the 1914 Day Clock
6:24–6:35 'We work less' chips, 6:40 Busy, 6:41 'So where did all that time go?'
7:38–7:50 2100 evidence cards; 8:03–8:14 refill bar, ENERGY/MONEY strikes, 'A day you actually remember'
8:16–8:28 close; 9:04–9:18 like/share/subscribe, Sun teaser, ASK/WONDER/REPEAT; 9:19–9:34 end screen (15.4 s, EXAMPLE comment labelled correctly)
Facts on screen match the narration everywhere checked (years, 16 h vs 10 days, 93 min, 1,354 h, 10.2 bn, 300 m, 56 of 61, 15 h)
Title-safe: the persistent header and HUD sit 14–15 px from the top, 18 px from the bottom and 30–32 px from the sides (480-wide scale); no typos found
not_verified: Sub-second timing: frames are 1 per second (each at about N+0.47 s). Flicker, 1–3 frame glitches and exact crossfade overlaps were inferred from source cue math, not seen frame by frame.

Audio was not listened to: SFX timing comes from build_final.py CUES and timeline-by-second.txt, not the rendered waveform. Loudness, mix balance, ducking, clipping and real A/V sync drift were not checked.
Fine legibility, colour and banding at full 1080p (review was on 480-px frames).
That the master was built from the current Tc*.tsx sources is assumed. Every empty-frame prediction from the code matched the frames, which supports this.
